message.content:
Below is an overview of the key rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas. These rules come from the Texas Property Code (Title 2, Chapter 91) and related statutes. If you need more detailed guidance—especially if your situation involves a dispute with a landlord—you may want to consult a lawyer or a local tenant‑rights organization. | Area | What the law says | Practical take‑away | |------|-------------------|---------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be held in a separate account and returned within **30 days** after the lease ends, unless the landlord gives a written itemized list of deductions. | Keep a copy of the receipt and the written agreement that states how much the deposit is. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For a month‑to‑month tenancy, landlords must give **30 days’ written notice** before raising rent or terminating the tenancy.
• For a fixed‑term lease, the landlord cannot raise rent during the term unless the lease itself allows it. | Ask for a written notice if your landlord wants to change the rent or end the tenancy. | | **Habitability & Repairs** | • Landlords must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition and maintain essential services (heat, hot water, plumbing, electrical).
• Tenants may withhold rent only if the landlord fails to repair major problems after being notified. | Document any repairs needed (photos, emails). Notify the landlord in writing first. | | **Eviction Process** | • A landlord must serve a **30‑day notice** for nonpayment of rent or a **60‑day notice** for other reasons (e.g., violation of lease terms).
• After the notice period, the landlord files a **Petition for Eviction** in court. The tenant has a chance to respond. | Do not ignore notices; respond promptly. | | **Right to Privacy** | • Landlords may enter the rental unit only for emergencies, to make necessary repairs, or to show the unit to prospective tenants or buyers, but they must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours). | Keep a log of all entries. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Under federal Fair Housing laws and Texas statutes, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | Report discrimination to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or the Texas Attorney General. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a month‑to‑month lease with **30 days’ written notice**.
• For a fixed‑term lease, the tenant may break the lease early only if the landlord agrees or if there is a “constructive eviction” (the landlord makes the unit uninhabitable). | Get any early termination agreement in writing. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas does **not** have statewide rent control. | Rent increases are governed by the lease agreement and the 30‑day notice rule. | ### How to Protect Yourself 1. **Get everything in writing** – leases, receipts, notices, repair requests. 2. **Keep records** – photos of damage, copies of correspondence, maintenance logs. 3. **Know the timeline** – 30‑day notice for rent changes, 60‑day notice for ending a lease. 4. **Respond promptly** – if you receive a notice, reply in writing and keep a copy. 5. **Seek help if needed** – contact the Texas Attorney General’s Office, local tenant‑rights groups, or a qualified attorney. --- #### Useful Resources | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumer-protection | | Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs | https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us/ | | HUD – Fair Housing Complaint Center | https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp/complaint_center | | Local tenant‑rights organizations (search “tenant rights Texas”) | — | If you’re facing a specific issue—like a disputed security deposit, a potential eviction, or a repair problem—feel free to describe it, and I can give more tailored advice or help draft a letter to your landlord.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are my rights as a tenant in the state of Texas?" They want information about tenant rights. We can provide general info. But we might also offer to generate a contract. The user didn't ask for a contract. So no need to call the function. Just answer. Provide overview: security deposit limits, notice requirements, habitability, eviction process, etc. Also mention resources like Texas Attorney General website, local housing agencies. Provide citations maybe. No function needed.
